comparison.objective: Tighten a tourniquet windlass against rollback until a gauge is green, snap the rod into its clip, and release it; candidate sets and jam-nut-locks a gripper opening stop before cycling it.
comparison.physical_skill: Both involve loaded rotary adjustment and locking, but PR-1026 requires windlass regrasping and rod snap-in while preserving band tension; candidate requires simultaneous coaxial driver counterholding and thin-nut wrench tightening without shifting a precision screw setting.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1026 succeeds when pressure is at least 250 mmHg, the rod is clipped, and the robot clears it for one second; candidate requires a 90° retained stop, at most 2° drift across three cycles, both nuts retained, and one-second 30 mm clearance.
comparison.reason: Shared adjust-lock-release primitives do not erase the meaningful difference between regrasping and clipping a rollback-loaded windlass versus two-tool screw/jam-nut countertorque followed by repeated functional retention testing; the record supplies complete thresholds and failure tiers.
